headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure between n8n and semantica.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and execute workflow nodes, while semantica can ingest local files, web pages, email, and MCP resources. If n8n passes semantica-generated content through files or shared channels, semantica’s inputs can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF n8n writes semantica-produced content into a shared file or queue
IF semantica parses n8n output as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared-file handoff between the two systems
Add provenance tags to every inter-agent payload
Require a human approval step before semantica executes n8n-generated instructions
Restrict n8n workflows to non-executable text outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem data, and semantica explicitly touches enterprise data, contracts, decision records, audit trails, and secrets-bearing sources like email and databases. n8n has broad network egress and handles per-credential secrets, so a shared workspace or credential path can leak sensitive data from one agent into the other or onward to external services.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or mounted volume
IF n8n workflows send file contents to external integrations
IF semantica ingests secrets-bearing sources into its shared context graph
mitigations: Separate storage volumes and credentials per agent
Block n8n from forwarding raw file contents to third-party nodes
Limit semantica connectors to non-sensitive sources during pairing
Rotate any shared secrets used by both systems
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the filesystem and execute shell commands on the server, while semantica can also write files, modify git state, and use MCP/CLI. That creates overlapping write authority over shared mutable resources; without explicit locking, concurrent edits can corrupt files, repositories, or workflow state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF n8n Execute Command and semantica CLI/MCP run concurrently
IF no external lock or lease is enforced
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and repositories
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Disable git mutation in one agent during shared runs
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node orchestrates tools, and semantica’s deterministic graph/provenance layer can still consume upstream outputs as inputs. If n8n-generated facts or actions are treated as authoritative by semantica, errors can cascade into downstream records, decisions, or automated integrations without a verification gate.
conditions: IF semantica ingests n8n outputs without validation
IF n8n workflows emit unverified facts that semantica stores as provenance
IF either agent triggers downstream actions from the other’s output
mitigations: Insert a verification step before semantica accepts n8n output
Mark n8n outputs as untrusted until checked
Require source citations for any transferred facts
Limit downstream automation to read-only review mode
requires-engineering: implement cross-agent provenance validation

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles per-credential secrets and server-side workflow data, while semantica touches enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and multiple external sources. The profiles do not state matching residency, retention, or subject-rights controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible, but not proven. The risk is lower than high because no explicit cross-border or regulated-data violation is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data flows through both systems under different retention policies
IF one agent stores audit trails longer than the other
IF EU or PHI data is routed through a non-compliant connector
mitigations: Inventory data classes before pairing
Align retention settings across both systems
Restrict regulated data to one agent only
Review connector residency settings
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared compliance policy
